Reference Lists in a Paper That Does Not Exist: A Worked Example

Ada Placeholder, Bruno Example and Cora Sample Department of Invented Studies, Nowhere University
Abstract

We describe a paper written only to be looked at. It has an introduction, a short method and a reference list of fourteen entries, and none of it is real: the authors, their university, the cited papers and the venues that published them were all made up for screenshots of a reference checker.

Every name, title, venue and identifier on this page is fictional. Any resemblance to a real person or a real paper is a coincidence.

1 Introduction

Counting imaginary sheep is an old problem [1], and gradients that do not exist have been catalogued before [2, 11]. Kettles [3], lemonade stands [4] and paper boats [5] have all served as benchmarks, and so, recursively, have benchmarks themselves [14].

2 Method

We fold each reference into a lantern [7], shelve it with very small robots [8] and read the result aloud in a quiet library [9].
